title: Merge sort
summary: Split the array in half until each part has one value, then merge the sorted halves back together.

checkpoints.text: The calls kept splitting: 0 to 5, then 0 to 2, then 0 to 1, then 0 to 0. A part with one value is already sorted, so this call returns at once. Look at the stack panel: every waiting call remembers its own `left` and `right`.
Cells 0 and 1 were merged into 27 38: the first sorted pair.
Merging 27 38 43 with 3 9 82. The fronts of the two halves are compared, and the smaller one, 3, is copied into `temp`.
The final merge is complete in `temp` (3 9 27 38 43 82), and it is copied back into the array one cell at a time.
3 9 27 38 43 82. The array is halved about log₂ n times, and each level of merging touches all n values, so merge sort is O(n log n) in every case. The price is the extra `temp` array.
